name: Third Way
summary: The Third Way is the 1990s centre-left project of the US New Democrats, Blair's New Labour and Schroeder's Neue Mitte, set out in Giddens's writing and the 1999 Blair-Schroeder paper. It keeps market economies and fiscal discipline and drops state ownership, high taxes and equality of outcome, while keeping an active government that invests in education and skills, ties benefits to work and responsibility, and takes crime seriously. It describes itself as beyond the dogmas of left and right, pro-trade and pro-Europe.
scope: The 1990s project known as the Third Way (also the New Centre or Neue Mitte): Clinton's New Democrat and DLC programme, Blair's New Labour as set out in his 1998 pamphlet, the 1999 Blair-Schroeder paper and Giddens's theory of it, as the defining sources (Dionne, Judis and Teixeira, Wiesenthal) describe it. Excludes older third-way usages (Swedish social democracy between capitalism and communism, distributism) and the later centrist think tanks. Governments' records are not used: the parties governed among others and the texts, not the governments' acts, define the ideology here.
